narrative.overview:
Adonissimo is Lorenz Anthony Salvador’s personal nickname and the lead wordmark for his internship and full-stack developer portfolio. The implemented world expands the established Hyrule field journal into Tears of the Kingdom settings: open sky and pale stone, a jade Zonai workshop, warm fields, and cool mineral Depths. Shared serif headings, local sans controls, gold emphasis and consistent navigation make these places one interface. The owner’s name and full-stack focus accompany the brand; work and honest explanations provide the proof.

The character is playful, adventurous and visually careful. Four original painted realm scenes, four transparent relic/botanical PNGs, graphic chapter headings, complete scenic footer cutouts and decorative geometry establish place; familiar controls, compact content groups and readable articles support browsing. The manual book-cover welcome, route page turns and optional user-triggered music retain the earlier cinematic signature. The site remains visibly identified as an unofficial fan portfolio.

This is a source-observed design record, merged from the incumbent design and the completed branding interview. No browser, design engine or detector was available for this documentation pass. The earlier independent finish review returned **recapture** because required desktop/mobile screenshots were missing; that visual gate remains open. The operator subsequently supplied passing tests, TypeScript, ESLint and production-build results for 3.3.1. The 3.6.0 update passes the 83 existing Node tests and isolated source/lifecycle checks here, while its full build and browser verification still need the operator's environment. Source inspection does not establish rendered appearance, responsiveness, live backend behavior or full accessibility.

Source 3.7.0 uses transparent foreground art, coordinated actual text/image/book/rune transitions and semantic magical route sounds. Two transparent edits were generated; sky/Depths reuse existing alpha artwork after the generation limit. The visible motion toggle is removed; full motion is the default. OS preferences remain automatic. Full browser, build and listening verification remain required.

Source 3.8.0 repairs the explicit full-motion gate even under an OS reduced preference, restores the original wide PNG footer and connects Enter to the rune reveal. Ambient leaves/motes/background breathing and a desktop winged fairy cursor/light trail use fixed pools with hidden/blur cleanup. The expanded dock can pause ambient effects independently. 95 source tests and isolated TSX event/lifecycle checks pass; browser/build/audio/performance verification remains required.

Source 3.9.0 adapts compact navigation, forms, project rows and the audio dock for phones. Speed-responsive fairy wings keep fluttering at rest. Day/night and realm-specific rays, mist and a fuller leaf field use bounded desktop/touch budgets. The Triforce opening has an original forest prelude that attempts autoplay without a sound button, with trusted-gesture retry and clean entry handoff. 98 Node tests and 129 syntax transforms pass; real browser/audio/performance/build verification is still required.

Source 3.10.0 portals the shared animated fairy into the native welcome dialog. Fuller fog layers drift calmly across the opening and pages, with 48-second rays and 52–84-second mist legs. Existing PNG stone/forest mural wings protect the central copy. Enter releases a white/gold Triforce zoom over 820ms. Image generation was usage-limited, so no new illustration is claimed. 101 Node tests, 130 syntax transforms and isolated real-component checks pass; browser/build/listening/performance gates remain open.

Source 3.11.0 adds a connected curved 3D paper sheet and moving shadow, with eight strips/940ms desktop and five/720ms compact. Prompt navigation, flat fallback, cancellation and the 3.10 welcome/atmosphere remain. 105 Node tests, 132 syntax transforms and isolated component checks pass; browser paint/performance and full build remain unverified.

Source 3.11.1 explicitly loads the selected visible backdrop and hero eagerly, gives the hero high fetch priority, and declares root smooth scrolling for Next router integration. The visual world and motion timings remain. 105 tests and 132 syntax transforms pass; browser warning verification/full build remain local.

Source 3.12.0 makes the atmosphere visible using three textured foreground cloud depths and stronger realm/day-night light shafts. The shared bounded canvas portals into the welcome and continues across routes, protecting reading and keeping calm drift. Two quality textures are cached; hidden/pause/cleanup stop work. 109 tests, 135 syntax transforms and isolated component lifecycle checks pass; real browser/contrast/performance/full-build gates remain open.
keyCharacteristics: Four context-selected settings with one shared day/night preference.
Forest/parchment heritage extended through sky stone, jade and mineral ink.
Locally loaded editorial serif with compact, familiar sans-serif controls.
Tonal layering, thin rules, restrained corners and bounded interaction feedback.
Recognizable Zelda identity, original fan art and truthful portfolio states.
Manual-entry welcome, optional book turns and independently controlled music/effects.
dos: Do keep Adonissimo, Lorenz’s name and full-stack focus together in the initial content group.
Do select the realm by context and preserve the user’s independent day/night preference.
Do use semantic palette variables, the local serif/sans pairing and shared control geometry.
Do keep Projects and Contact easy to find with familiar labels and one clear primary action per group.
Do preserve truthful planned/published states, visible focus, labeled controls and reduced-motion/manual-audio paths.
Do use recognizable Zelda emblems and original fan artwork consistently, with decorative glyphs hidden from assistive technology.
Do retain the unofficial fan identification in the footer and keep source checks separate from browser/live-service evidence.
donts: Don't replace the explicitly requested Zelda identity with generic fantasy symbols.
Don't turn every paragraph or row into a raised card, or add glass panels, fake grain, neon UI glow, gradient text or unrelated technology branding.
Don't use decorative glyphs or fantasy-only language as the sole navigation or operational label.
Don't use tiny text, clipped prose, excessive blank gaps or repeated ornament to manufacture compactness or fill missing content.
Don't invent project outcomes, professional experience, metrics, contact details, résumé links or screenshots.
Don't make reading or navigation depend on a long scene, automatic audio or decorative animation completing.
Don't describe source inspection or the recapture disposition as verified appearance, responsiveness, production readiness or full accessibility.
